newsitem.title: USA: Central Soya to accept Roundup Ready soybeans.
newsitem.headline: Central Soya to accept Roundup Ready soybeans.

text.p: Central Soya Co Inc on Friday said it planned to accept soybeans grown from genetically altered Roundup Ready seed at all six of its soybean crushing plants, but one Ohio grain elevator will not accept them.
"This will impact less than one percent of the beans Central Soya will buy from this year's crop," William Campbell, vice president of processing, said in a statement on Friday.
"At this (Ohio) facility, we are isolating a small quantity of non-genetically modified soybeans for purposes of comparative testing in further processed products."
Archer Daniels Midland Co and Cargill Inc said Thursday they would also accept the soybeans which were altered to allow farmers to safely spray Monsanto Co's popular Roundup brand herbicide.
The European Union in March approved for import soybeans grown from the seeds.

But a European food retailers' and wholesalers' group on Thursday warned that their members would avoid U.S. soybeans unless farmers separated the altered strains and gene-altered soy products were labeled.
USDA Under Secretary Gene Moos on Thursday repeated the U.S. stance that labelling for transgenic products would be both unnecessary and unworkable.
"There's no need for labelling. We see no reason why labelling should be required and we think it impossible on top of that," Moos told Reuters.
About one to two percent of the 1996 U.S. soybean crop, or 1.5 million tonnes, is transgenic, said Jim Hershey of the American Soybean Association in St. Louis.
Monsanto spokeswoman Karen Marshall on Friday said that figure would likely rise next year as more Roundup Ready seed becomes available.
"We think that the crop next year will be limited only by the amount of seed available," Marshall said.
She predicted between five million and 10 million acres of Roundup Ready soybeans would be planted next year.
